answer: One defense is bonded identity: before an agent can trade, it must lock a meaningful stake that is slashed if it misbehaves or is proven to be a duplicate. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of stakes, like trying to buy a walnut harvest and a saffron crop with pocket change — the expense scales linearly while honest agents pay once. A bridge of independent attestors verifies each identity against prior work, so a Sybil swarm cannot simply clone one good reputation for free.
